title: Wall Street Slips as Warsh Opens Door to a Rate Hike
content: US stocks fell on Friday after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh used his Jackson Hole address to warn the central bank would "have work to do" if inflation failed to head back towards 2%, the clearest signal yet that a rate rise is on the table. The S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,711.76 as traders priced in a roughly 57% chance of a September hike, though the index still eked out a small weekly gain.
summary: The S&P 500 fell on Friday after Fed Chair Warsh hinted at a possible rate hike, though the index still closed the week higher.
context:
• Kevin Warsh took the Fed chair earlier in 2026 with a mandate to restore the central bank's inflation-fighting credibility after a stretch of sticky price pressures.

• Core inflation has stalled well above target, leaving the Fed debating whether policy is restrictive enough rather than when to ease.

• Equities entered the week near record highs, with valuations stretched and acutely sensitive to any upward shift in the expected path of rates.
happened:
• Warsh said the Fed would "have work to do" without greater confidence inflation is falling to 2%, the closest he has come to endorsing a hike.

• The S&P 500 ended Friday down 0.25% at 7,711.76 and the Nasdaq lost 0.52% to 26,402.42, weighed by chipmakers.

• Market-implied odds of a September rate increase jumped to about 57% from roughly 35% a day earlier, according to CME data.
implications:
• A hawkish Fed caps the upside for richly valued equities and shifts leadership away from long-duration growth names.

• The September FOMC meeting becomes a genuine two-way risk event, raising the premium on hedging into the autumn.

• Any hot data print between now and the decision could harden the case for a hike and deepen the equity pullback.
importance:
• A Fed openly weighing hikes reverses the easing narrative that underpinned much of 2026's rally.

• Index concentration in mega-cap technology magnifies the hit from higher discount rates.

• The episode resets expectations for the terminal rate and the cost of capital across markets.

title: Short-Dated Treasuries Sell Off on September Hike Bets
content: Front-end Treasuries slumped after Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks, with the two-year yield jumping 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest in a month, as traders repriced the odds of a near-term rate rise. The move flattened the curve as longer maturities lagged, with the 10-year up 5 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year barely changed at 5.206%.
summary: The two-year Treasury yield surged 11 basis points to 4.34% as markets priced in a possible September rate hike.
context:
• Rate-sensitive two-year notes track the expected path of Fed policy most closely, making them the sharpest gauge of hike expectations.

• The long end has been under separate pressure all year from heavy government supply and fiscal-sustainability worries.

• Money markets had been leaning towards a hold or cut, leaving positioning exposed to a hawkish surprise.
happened:
• The two-year yield rose 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest level in about a month.

• The 10-year yield climbed 5 basis points to 4.72% while the 30-year edged up 1.6 basis points to 5.206%, flattening the curve.

• Fed funds futures moved to imply roughly a 57% probability of a September hike, up from about 35% before Warsh spoke.
implications:
• A flatter curve tightens financial conditions and squeezes leveraged carry and duration trades.

• Higher front-end yields lift funding costs across credit, mortgages and corporate borrowing.

• Should the Fed hold in September, the sharp repricing leaves room for an equally sharp reversal.
importance:
• The two-year is the market's real-time verdict on Fed policy, and it has swung decisively hawkish.

• Curve shape drives bank margins, credit spreads and the relative appeal of bonds versus equities.

• Rate volatility bleeds into every other asset class, from FX to crypto.

title: Dollar Rebounds as Rate-Hike Odds Climb
content: The US dollar rallied on Friday, with the DXY index rising 0.6% to 99.66 as Warsh's hawkish tone revived the greenback's yield appeal after a soft stretch. The bounce reversed part of the currency's recent slide, driven by rekindled expectations that US rates could rise while other major central banks stay on hold or ease.
summary: The dollar index rose 0.6% to 99.66 as hawkish Fed signals restored the greenback's interest-rate advantage.
context:
• The dollar had weakened through August on doubts over Fed independence and a narrowing US yield premium.

• Currency direction has become tightly coupled to shifts in the expected Fed path relative to peers.

• A softer dollar earlier in the month had helped fuel gains in gold, crypto and emerging-market assets.
happened:
• The DXY dollar index climbed 0.6% to 99.66 as short-dated Treasury yields spiked.

• The move followed Warsh's suggestion that the Fed may need to tighten further to tame inflation.

• The rebound widened the US rate advantage just as several peer central banks are seen holding or cutting.
implications:
• A firmer dollar tightens global financial conditions and pressures commodity and emerging-market currencies.

• Dollar strength is a headwind for US multinationals' overseas earnings and for gold.

• A September hold would likely unwind the bounce, keeping the currency hostage to each Fed data point.
importance:
• The dollar sets the terms for global trade, commodity pricing and cross-border capital flows.

• Its direction shapes returns on every non-dollar asset for international investors.

• The swing shows how completely FX is now being driven by the Fed hike debate.

title: Bitcoin Retreats From $81,000 as Warsh Chills Risk Appetite
content: Bitcoin briefly topped $81,000 during the week, its highest since mid-May, before Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech knocked it back below $78,000. Despite the late pullback the token was still up around 28% for August, on track for its best month since late 2024, with ether also finishing the week higher.
summary: Bitcoin hit an intraday high above $81,000 before sliding on hawkish Fed signals, though it remained up about 28% for August.
context:
• Digital assets have traded increasingly as a high-beta play on dollar liquidity and the expected Fed path.

• Spot bitcoin ETFs remain a dominant flow channel, amplifying rallies and reversals alike.

• A strong August rally had been powered by improving liquidity expectations and heavy institutional inflows.
happened:
• Bitcoin reached an intraday high near $81,142 on Friday before reversing as Warsh's remarks hit risk assets.

• The token slid roughly 3% to around $77,844 by the weekend, paring but not erasing its monthly advance.

• Bitcoin was still up about 28% for August, its strongest month since November 2024, while ether rose about 5% on the week.
implications:
• Crypto's tight link to the Fed leaves it exposed if hike bets keep firming into September.

• A stronger dollar and higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding tokens.

• Sustained ETF demand could cushion pullbacks, but leverage leaves the market prone to sharp swings.
importance:
• The reversal underscores how quickly macro-policy signals now dictate crypto direction.

• Bitcoin's monthly gain shows digital assets remain a core risk-appetite barometer.

• Crypto-linked equities trade as high-beta proxies, spreading the volatility into stock portfolios.

title: Gold Holds Near Record Above $4,600
content: Gold steadied around $4,600 an ounce on Friday, holding near record territory after a blistering run that has lifted the metal roughly 15% this month. Persistent inflation, geopolitical friction in the Middle East and central-bank buying have kept demand firm even as a late-week dollar bounce capped the advance.
summary: Gold held near a record around $4,600 an ounce, up roughly 15% on the month on inflation and geopolitical demand.
context:
• Bullion has rallied more than 25% since early 2025 as investors sought a hedge against sticky inflation and policy uncertainty.

• Central-bank purchases and safe-haven flows have provided a persistent structural bid.

• Escalating Middle East tensions have added a fresh geopolitical premium through August.
happened:
• Spot gold traded around $4,600–$4,630 an ounce on Friday, close to record highs.

• The metal is up about 15% in August, one of its strongest months of the rally.

• A 0.6% rise in the dollar late in the week trimmed gains without breaking the uptrend.
implications:
• Further dollar strength or higher real yields could stall the rally, given gold pays no income.

• Continued central-bank buying and geopolitical risk provide a durable floor under prices.

• Record bullion prices lift margins and equity valuations across the gold-mining sector.
importance:
• Gold's surge is a vote of no confidence in the durability of disinflation and fiat stability.

• The metal's strength signals persistent demand for hedges against policy and geopolitical risk.

• Bullion's move ripples through miners, ETFs and central-bank reserve strategy.

title: Brent Slides More Than 5% on Weak Demand
content: Brent crude fell towards $89 a barrel on Friday, heading for a weekly loss of more than 5% as softening Chinese demand and easing supply fears outweighed lingering tensions around Iran. West Texas Intermediate slipped to about $83, down over 4% on the week, after the IEA and OPEC trimmed their 2026 demand forecasts.
summary: Brent crude fell more than 5% on the week to around $89 as weakening Chinese demand offset Middle East supply risk.
context:
• Oil had been supported through much of the summer by Middle East tensions and disruption fears around the Strait of Hormuz.

• China's crude imports have fallen sharply year on year amid weaker refining, a fuel-export ban and rising EV adoption.

• Both the IEA and OPEC have cut their 2026 demand outlooks, shifting the balance towards oversupply.
happened:
• Brent slipped to about $89.3 a barrel on Friday, extending its weekly loss beyond 5%.

• WTI fell to roughly $83, down about 4% on the week.

• Traders reframed the Iran standoff as an economic rather than immediate supply threat as flows through Hormuz improved.
implications:
• Cheaper crude eases headline inflation pressure, complicating the hawkish rates narrative.

• Weak Chinese demand and rising non-OPEC supply point to a softer price floor into year-end.

• Lower oil squeezes energy-sector earnings even as it relieves consumers and industry.
importance:
• Oil is a primary input to global inflation and a bellwether for world demand.

• The demand-led drop signals genuine concern about the health of the Chinese and global economy.

• Falling crude reshapes the outlook for energy equities, inflation and central-bank policy alike.

title: European Stocks Rebound Friday as French Fiscal Fears Linger
content: European bourses closed higher on Friday, led by a 1% gain in France's CAC 40 as the index clawed back losses driven by anxiety over the country's budget and political outlook. The rebound followed a bruising week in which French banks slid 4–5% and the CAC touched a one-month low on renewed fiscal worries, even as Germany's DAX held near record highs.
summary: European stocks rose on Friday, with the CAC 40 up 1%, but France's fiscal and political worries weighed on the week.
context:
• French assets have been dogged for months by concerns over the budget deficit and political fragility ahead of next year's presidential race.

• The DAX and Euro STOXX 50 have traded near record highs in 2026, led by banks and semiconductor names.

• European equities remain sensitive to the global bond-yield backdrop and the US rates debate.
happened:
• The CAC 40 rose about 1% on Friday as French stocks reversed the prior session's slump.

• Earlier in the week the CAC fell roughly 1.7% to a one-month low, with BNP Paribas, Société Générale and Crédit Agricole each down 4–5%.

• The STOXX Europe 600 had dropped 0.7% on Thursday to 651.85, its worst session in about a month, before Friday's broad rebound.
implications:
• France's fiscal and political risk premium could keep its banks and bonds volatile into the autumn.

• A hawkish Fed and firmer dollar may pressure European exporters and rate-sensitive sectors.

• Record-high German and euro-zone benchmarks leave the region exposed to any global risk-off shift.
importance:
• France sits at the core of euro-zone credit and any wobble carries systemic weight.

• Bank-sector swings are a key barometer of confidence in European financial stability.

• Divergence between a strong DAX and a shaky CAC highlights widening intra-Europe risk.

title: Nikkei Hits Record as Asia Rides Nvidia's AI Beat
content: Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 0.41% to a record 66,405.56 on Friday as blockbuster Nvidia earnings lifted sentiment across Asian technology shares. The gains were uneven, however, with South Korean chipmakers among the region's sharpest fallers and mainland Chinese benchmarks slipping despite firmer industrial-profit data.
summary: Japan's Nikkei hit a record on Nvidia-driven tech optimism, though South Korean chip stocks and Chinese benchmarks lagged.
context:
• Asian equity direction is closely tied to the AI investment cycle and the fortunes of the global semiconductor supply chain.

• Nvidia's results are a bellwether for regional chip and hardware makers from Tokyo to Taipei and Seoul.

• Chinese markets remain weighed by uneven growth even as industrial profits keep rising.
happened:
• The Nikkei 225 rose 0.41% to a record 66,405.56, buoyed by Nvidia's nearly 9% surge in the prior US session.

• South Korea suffered one of the region's steepest drops as investors sold major technology shares, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed roughly flat at 25,584.79.

• China's Shanghai Composite fell 0.11% to 3,952.18 even as industrial profits rose 17.6% year on year in the first seven months of 2026.
implications:
• Continued AI capex momentum should keep supporting Japanese and Taiwanese chip-related equities.

• A stronger dollar and higher US yields could cap gains for export-heavy Asian markets.

• Divergence between Japan's records and Korea's weakness underscores how stock-specific the AI trade has become.
importance:
• The Nikkei's record shows the AI boom is powering equity gains well beyond Wall Street.

• Asia's chip supply chain is central to the global technology cycle and index performance.

• Uneven regional moves signal that AI optimism is not lifting all boats equally.

title: Nvidia Revenue Doubles to $96bn as AI Demand Roars On
content: Nvidia reported second-quarter revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year earlier, with data-centre sales surging 117% to $89 billion and guidance for the current quarter of about $108 billion sailing past forecasts. The results reaffirmed that spending on AI infrastructure remains torrid, sending Nvidia shares up around 9% and rallying chipmakers worldwide.
summary: Nvidia's quarterly revenue doubled to $96.2 billion with data-centre sales up 117%, and it guided above expectations.
context:
• Nvidia is the single most important stock for the AI trade and a heavy weight in US and global indices.

• Investors have watched each report for evidence that hyperscaler AI capex is holding up.

• The company's outlook excludes any data-centre compute revenue from China amid export restrictions.
happened:
• Revenue rose 106% year on year to $96.2 billion, with data-centre revenue up 117% to $89 billion and gross margin at 75%.

• Nvidia guided to roughly $108 billion in current-quarter revenue, above Wall Street estimates, with chief executive Jensen Huang forecasting about 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.

• The shares climbed around 9% following the report, lifting Broadcom and other semiconductor names.
implications:
• Robust guidance underpins the AI capex thesis and supports elevated valuations across the chip sector.

• Heavy index reliance on Nvidia means its results move the entire market, cutting both ways.

• Excluding China from the outlook leaves upside optionality but also highlights geopolitical risk.
importance:
• Nvidia's numbers are the clearest read on whether the AI investment boom is still accelerating.

• As the market's largest weight, its swings drive index-level returns and volatility.

• The beat re-anchored sentiment for the entire global semiconductor complex.

title: Core PCE Stuck at 3.3% Keeps Fed on Edge
content: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge showed core PCE prices rose 3.3% in the year to July, unchanged from June and well above the 2% target, reinforcing the case for a hawkish policy stance. Headline PCE held at 3.7% while personal income and spending both came in firmer than expected, underlining that price pressures are proving stubborn.
summary: Core PCE inflation held at 3.3% year on year in July, staying well above target and supporting a hawkish Fed.
context:
• PCE is the inflation measure the Fed targets, making it the most consequential data point for the rate path.

• Core inflation has stalled above 3% for months, frustrating hopes of a smooth return to 2%.

• The print landed days before Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, framing the hawkish message.
happened:
• Core PCE rose 0.2% on the month and held at 3.3% year on year in July, in line with forecasts.

• Headline PCE stayed at 3.7% annually, while personal income rose 0.4% and spending gained 0.2%, both above expectations.

• Services prices climbed 0.3% on the month even as goods prices dipped 0.1%.
implications:
• Sticky core inflation hands the Fed cover to weigh a September rate hike rather than a cut.

• Resilient income and spending suggest demand is strong enough to keep price pressures alive.

• Persistently above-target inflation risks entrenching higher-for-longer expectations across markets.
importance:
• PCE is the number the Fed acts on, so a stalled reading directly shapes policy risk.

• Above-target inflation undercuts the case for easing that markets had leaned on.

• The data anchor the hawkish repricing now rippling through rates, FX and equities.
